item.subject: Advanced Mathematics
item.stem:
Which of the following graphs has these features:
f'(0) > 0, f'(1) < 0, and f''(x) is always negative?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Downward-opening curve entirely below the x-axis]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Upward-opening curve entirely above the x-axis]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Curve with a maximum on the y-axis and a minimum for x > 1]

options.label: E
options.text: [Image: Curve with a local minimum for x < 0 and a local maximum between 0 and 1]

item.figure_description:
Five Cartesian coordinate systems labeled A through E, each with a horizontal x-axis and a vertical y-axis, and a tick mark labeled 1 on the positive x-axis:
- Graph A shows a curve concave downward everywhere, located entirely below the x-axis, with its vertex (maximum) between x = 0 and x = 1. At x = 0 the slope is positive, and at x = 1 the slope is negative.
- Graph B shows a curve concave upward everywhere, located entirely above the x-axis, with its vertex (minimum) between x = 0 and x = 1.
- Graph C shows a curve with a local maximum on the y-axis at x = 0, which decreases, crosses the x-axis, reaches a local minimum to the right of x = 1, and then curves upward.
- Graph D shows a curve that decreases strictly from left to right, concave downward everywhere, crossing the y-axis with a negative slope and crossing the x-axis to the left of x = 1.
- Graph E shows a curve that has a local minimum for x < 0, increases through the y-axis with a positive slope at x = 0, reaches a local maximum between x = 0 and x = 1, and decreases through x = 1.
item.calibration: Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it.
